title: Star Wars Is Coming to IMAX for the First Time Ever!
summary:
Have you ever watched Star Wars on a screen so big it feels like you're inside the movie? In 2027, that dream comes true. The original Star Wars — the one from 1977 — is coming to IMAX for the first time ever.

Why now? Because 2027 marks the 50th anniversary of Star Wars. The first movie hit theaters on May 25, 1977. George Lucas created a whole galaxy of heroes, villains, and lightsabers that changed movies forever.

To celebrate, Disney and Lucasfilm are releasing a newly restored version of the original film. It will show at IMAX locations starting February 19, 2027. And here's the cool part: it's apparently being shown without the "A New Hope" subtitle, without the Special Edition changes, and without CGI additions. That means Han Solo will once again fire his blaster at Greedo first — just like in 1977!

Some IMAX theaters will even show it on 70mm film, a rare format that uses actual physical film instead of digital. That's like listening to a vinyl record instead of a streaming playlist.

But wait, there's more. A brand-new Star Wars movie called Star Wars: Starfighter comes out on May 28, 2027. It stars Ryan Gosling as Kade Auberon, a cynical rogue with a mysterious past. The movie was filmed with special IMAX cameras and directed by Shawn Levy, who worked on Stranger Things and Deadpool & Wolverine.

So whether you're a lifelong fan or have never seen Star Wars, 2027 is the year to experience it on the biggest screen possible. May the Force be with you!
why_it_matters: Movies are something families and friends enjoy together, and this shows how a story from 50 years ago can still pull people into a giant cinema — maybe one you'll get to see on the big screen too.

background_read: George Lucas (the American filmmaker who created Star Wars) released the first movie in 1977, and it became one of the most famous films ever made.
IMAX is a chain of cinemas with screens far bigger than normal ones, often used for big event films and special re-releases.
In 1997, George Lucas changed some scenes for a 'Special Edition' — including the famous moment when Han Solo shoots Greedo, which fans argued about for years.
Article_Structure: WHO: Disney and Lucasfilm, plus actor Ryan Gosling and director Shawn Levy, who made the new film Star Wars: Starfighter.
WHAT: The original 1977 Star Wars is getting a restored IMAX release, and a brand-new Star Wars film is coming out the same year.
WHERE: IMAX cinemas, with some of them showing the film on 70mm film instead of digital.
WHY: To celebrate 50 years of Star Wars and let fans see the original film the way it looked in 1977, without the Special Edition changes.

perspectives.description: They are thrilled to see the original version without the Special Edition changes, and on a screen bigger than they've ever seen before.
Some say this is mostly nostalgia and a way for Disney to earn money from an old film, and not everyone lives near an IMAX cinema.
They note that anniversary re-releases are a common way studios keep classic films alive and introduce them to new, younger audiences.
